description: Page-sized build/redesign flow for one route or screen: enough research and design contract work to preserve quality without invoking the whole product lifecycle.

stages.purpose: Establish the page role, existing owner, user intent, constraints and reference evidence without expanding into unrelated product research.

gates.require: target route/screen, audience intent, preserve/forbidden constraints and source owner are explicit

stages.purpose: Define a concrete page-level composition and responsive behavior using the existing design language unless the task explicitly changes it.

gates.require: layout hierarchy, responsive transformation, component reuse and interaction states are concrete before implementation

stages.purpose: Implement the page-level change as reusable responsive code while preserving unrelated routes and shared owners.

gates.require: page acceptance criteria are mapped to the affected route and shared component regression surface

stages.purpose: Inspect the actual rendered page across representative viewports/states and verify shared-owner regressions without broadening into unrelated routes.

gates.require: target page is inspected at representative desktop/mobile widths and affected shared components show no material regression

policies.reason: Page rendered QA failed; return to implementation with focused root-cause review.
Page-role or owner assumptions were wrong; re-establish project truth before redesigning further.
Page work gained production risk; add system reality and verification specialists.
Diagnose repeated tool failure rather than blind retry.
Blocked page work needs decision reframing and constraint review.
